newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU diplomat says agreement near on stability pact.
newsitem.headline: EU diplomat says agreement near on stability pact.

text.p: European Union finance ministers were close to an agreement on a post-single currency stability pact on Monday, an EU diplomat said, adding that the ministers had now resolved most of the issues dividing them.

"They are in the box," the diplomat told Reuters, referring to the various elements of the agreement between European Union member states, which is aimed at ensuring that nations keep budgets in check after European monetary union starts in 1999.

The diplomat said the EU ministers now seemed to be heading towards middle ground on a key issue dividing member states -- a definition of the exceptional and temporary economic conditions which would allow a nation to overshoot the set deficit limit.

Going into the meeting, Germany had been demanding that an unusually strong recession be defined as a contraction of two percent in gross domestic product, while the European commission, backed by a number of other countries, had not wanted any figure to be specified.

"Countries are now prepared to (accept) some sort of a figure for what is an exceptional circumstance," the diplomat said. Under such a circumstance, a nations' budget deficit could exceed the agreed limit of three percent of GDP without penalty.

The diplomat also said that the EU finance ministers had agreed to a fixed level of fine which countries would face if they overshot the maximum permitted level. The initial fine would be 0.2 percent of GDP, rising to a maximum of 0.5 percent.
